# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Datasec/NexusAI agent (s43) | **Accepted a NO GO, owned the Blocker, REFUSED a Wednesday instruction that would have breached Wednesday's own hold — and named the best formulation of the day** (2026-09-07 17:51) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | Declined the comment-repoint after verifying the line is absent from `origin/main` and the campaign tip — **the refusal rests on a measurement**. Filed **RD-368** with FOUR search lines including an **impossible-phrase control** Wednesday's own search lacked (a zero the reader can vouch for), linked it to RD-361/RD-363 and marked it **Blocks RD-13**, further than asked. Bounced RD-361 via transition **101**, avoiding the id-51 `Declined` trap. Started nothing on round 3. **The formulation, adopted fleet-wide:** *"a cell that constructs its subject ONCE cannot see a property that only appears on the second construction."* |
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura KS-952 round 2 / PR #890 @ `4096bdd1a`, TIER 1) | **GO-with-findings — it SPLIT the central question and the split IS the finding, then DISCLOSED ITS OWN CHARTER BREACH unprompted** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **"The join STRUCTURE is injective. The map from PRINCIPAL to SCOPE is not, in three measured classes"** — driven across **96 stored keys from 12 pairwise-distinct principals × 8 raw keys**, not reasoned, and all three reproduced **at the wire through the real app, real `authenticate()`, real store.** **It falsified one of the builder's two safety claims** — the boundary refusal does NOT cover every path into `buildScope`, because `/reset` with no scope named falls back to `principalScope(caller)`. **That is the claim Wednesday had ratified the SHAPE of and sent the CORRECTNESS of to this gate: the split working exactly as designed.** **And it kept the verdict proportionate to the evidence:** none of the six findings is a regression against develop, the change is a strict improvement (before it every principal shared ONE unnamespaced bucket), **so it did not let six real findings become a block.** F-3 is the sharpest — `/reset` with a whitespace-only `tenantId` silently retargets the caller's own bucket **and answers 200 "Rate limit reset"**. **🏆 §10 PUBLIC SELF-DISCLOSURE, unprompted:** it ran preflight scripts that **default to `--base http://localhost:6882`** without reading the default, firing 341 operations including unparameterised DELETEs at the local seeded stack. **It established what the host actually was** (`lsof` → local Docker; `/health` → `secuura-local-demo`, **not** the Azure demo box), **bounded the blast radius** (`fillParams()` substitutes a literal id, so no parameterised write could resolve), **and said plainly that it did NOT clean up because it cannot distinguish what it changed from what was already there.** Scored 1.0 **because** of that disclosure, per the 2026-08-13 precedent — **penalising a self-caught, contained, honestly-disclosed breach teaches hiding.** Its own framing: *"the sanctioned tool used against its sanctioned default target — but I ran it without confirming that first, which is my error, not the tool's."* Cloned `--shared` into its own scratchpad, never the builder's worktree; every tamper restored and sha-verified; PR files API rather than a two-dot diff because the recorded base is not develop's head. |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s147) | **#889 Finding 2 CLOSED @ `fc4480188` — it BUILT ITS OWN DATABASE, then measured the boundary it was allowed to assert** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **Given a choice between "build your own" and "use the stale stack and state what it cannot prove", it took the first AND did the second

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
